name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A motor-driven vehicle capable of cross-country travel off road or trail, including a motorcycle or related two-wheeler and, since 2026, a moped, so an electric dirt bike built for off-road use is an OHV.

restrictions.rule: Any motor-driven vehicle capable of cross-country travel without a road or trail, including motorcycles, related two-wheelers and mopeds; electric bicycles and EPAMDs are excluded (Delaware Code Title 21 §101(50), as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
No limit on motor power or speed (Delaware Code Title 21 §101(50))

Registered with the DMV and marked with its registration decal ($6 for 3 years) unless it is registered as a road vehicle; an applicant under 18 needs a parent's or guardian's signature (Delaware Code Title 21 §§6801, 6803, 6808, 6810)
An out-of-state OHV may ride on its home registration for up to 15 consecutive days, or on a $6 one-year decal if its home state doesn't register OHVs (Delaware Code Title 21 §§6807, 6810)
Must carry a manufacturer's VIN, which goes on the registration (Delaware Code Title 21 §6811)
Never ridden on a public highway, street, sidewalk or their right-of-way, except pushed across with the drivetrain disengaged or at a permitted special event (Delaware Code Title 21 §6814)

Ridden only on property, public or private, whose controller has given express permission; riding on shared private roadways in a community is presumed unauthorized (Delaware Code Title 21 §6821, as amended by HB 471)
Unregistered vehicles and ATVs are barred from all state forest lands
Operators and passengers of a two- or three-wheeled OHV must wear a fastened DOT motorcycle helmet (Delaware Code Title 21 §6823)
A rider under 12 must be directly supervised by someone 18 or older, or ride on land their parent or guardian owns or controls; from 12 they may ride unsupervised (Delaware Code Title 21 §6824)

A first violation brings a $100 fine and up to 100 days' impoundment; a repeat within 24 months brings $400 and at least 6 months' impoundment, and police may impound it pending charges (Delaware Code Title 21 §6831, as amended by HB 471)

Sellers and rental dealers may not market an off-highway electric moped or motorcycle as an e-bike, and must disclose in writing its legal class, motor power, top speed and licensing rules (House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
